title: improve-dedicated-autoscaler-burst-controls-and-utilization-reporting
author: Anita Rao
description: Context: customers on Dedicated fleets saw unexpected latency spikes when short bursts of traffic exhausted token-based burst allowances; current observability lacked per-fleet burst utilization metrics which made incident triage slow. This PR implements more robust burst controls in the Dedicated autoscaler and adds first-class utilization reporting to make capacity decisions observable. Motivation: reduce tail latency during burst drains, prevent noisy tenants from starving long-running workloads, and provide operators with actionable metrics for tuning reserved capacity and burst budgets. Changes: 1) Autoscaler: introduce token-bucket-based burst policy with configurable fields (burst.max_tokens, burst.recharge_rate, burst.penalty_window_ms). The autoscaler now tracks "burst_usage_pct" and "burst_backlog_seconds" per-fleet and uses these signals for more conservative scale-down decisions and adaptive burst throttling. 2) Runtime: move token-bucket enforcement into the request router so burst checks occur before queuing on GPU workers; adds lightweight backpressure to reduce queue buildup. 3) Telemetry: emit new Prometheus metrics (redwood_dedicated_burst_usage_pct, redwood_dedicated_burst_backlog_seconds, redwood_dedicated_burst_tokens_remaining) and update the dedicated fleet overview dashboard. 4) CLI/Config: add backwards-compatible config schema v2 for dedicated-autoscaler; older configs are migrated automatically at startup with warnings. 5) Tests & Canary: unit tests for token-bucket edge cases, integration test that simulates burst drains, and a perf canary run on a staging fleet (results: 18% reduction in 95th percentile latency during bursts). Backwards compatibility and migration notes: config migration will log deprecated fields and translate to new defaults; operators can opt into strict mode to enforce schema validation. Rollout plan: staged canary -> 10% of production fleets -> full rollout with monitoring and automated rollback if burst_backlog_seconds > 30s for more than 5 minutes. Checklist: - [x] Design doc (ENG-2432) - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration canary run - [x] Dashboards & alerts updated - [x] Docs updated (docs/dedicated/autoscaler.md) Related: ENG-2432, ENG-2499, SUP-412
